name: The Gambia
tagline: A river with a country around it
summary: Three hundred kilometres of river with a strip of land either side, six hundred bird species, chimpanzees on the river islands, and the beaches that made it Europe's first West African destination.
when: November to April. Birding is best from November to February when the migrants are in.

entries.caption: The River
entries.description: The country is the river — three hundred kilometres of it, and a strip either bank.
entries.subject: the wide Gambia river with mangrove banks at sunset

entries.caption: Mangrove, Savanna and Gallery Forest
entries.description: Salt mangrove at the mouth, freshwater swamp in the middle, dry savanna at the top.
entries.subject: mangrove creeks and channels off the Gambia river

entries.caption: Six Hundred Bird Species
entries.description: In a country you can drive across in twenty minutes. It is one of the great birding places.
entries.subject: an Abyssinian roller on a branch in Gambian savanna

entries.caption: Chimps at Baboon Islands
entries.description: A rehabilitated chimpanzee population on river islands, watched from boats only.
entries.subject: chimpanzees on the bank of a Gambia river island

entries.caption: Flat
entries.description: The highest point is fifty-three metres. This is river country, not hill country.
entries.subject: flat savanna and a lone baobab in the upper river region

entries.caption: None
entries.description: No falls. The river drops so little across the country that the tide runs a hundred kilometres up it.
entries.subject: still water and reflected trees on the upper Gambia river

entries.caption: The Gambia Itself
entries.description: Tidal for half its length, and every town on it is a landing.
entries.subject: a ferry crossing the Gambia river at Farafenni

entries.caption: Eighty Kilometres of Atlantic
entries.description: Kotu, Kololi and Cape Point, and the quieter sand south towards Kartong.
entries.subject: a wide Atlantic beach with fishing boats at Tanji

entries.caption: Bijilo and Abuko
entries.description: Small forest reserves close to the coast, with colobus, vervets and a great deal of birdlife.
entries.subject: red colobus monkeys in the canopy at Bijilo forest

entries.caption: Upriver by Boat
entries.description: Four days up the river from Banjul to Janjanbureh, watching the country change.
entries.subject: a small river boat moving upstream past mangrove

entries.caption: Mandinka, Fula, Wolof, Jola
entries.description: Four main peoples in a country of three million, and a griot tradition across all of them.
entries.subject: a kora player performing at a Gambian village gathering

entries.caption: The Griots
entries.description: The Jali families hold the histories, and the kora is how they are told.
entries.subject: a Jali griot playing the kora outside a compound

entries.caption: Benachin and Domoda
entries.description: Benachin — one-pot rice — and domoda, groundnut stew with lamb.
entries.subject: a shared bowl of benachin rice with fish and vegetables

entries.caption: Kankurang
entries.description: A masked figure of the Mandinka initiation, and a UNESCO-listed tradition.
entries.subject: the Kankurang masked figure in red bark and leaves

entries.caption: Batik, Carving and Baskets
entries.description: Tie-dye and batik along the coast, and coiled baskets from the upper river.
entries.subject: batik cloth and coiled baskets at a craft market stall

entries.caption: Kunta Kinteh Island
entries.description: A slaving island in the river, eroding, and the reason a great many people come.
entries.subject: the ruined fort on Kunta Kinteh Island in the Gambia river

entries.caption: Stone Circles and the Slave Route
entries.description: The Wassu stone circles are a thousand years old; the river route is four hundred.
entries.subject: the standing laterite stone circles at Wassu

entries.caption: Banjul and Serekunda
entries.description: A small capital on an island, and the much larger market town that outgrew it.
entries.subject: the Albert Market and crowds in Banjul

entries.caption: Colonial and Compound
entries.description: Colonial Banjul, and the walled family compounds that are the real unit of Gambian building.
entries.subject: a walled family compound with a swept yard and mango tree

entries.caption: The Fish Landing at Tanji
entries.description: The boats come in mid-afternoon and the beach becomes a market in twenty minutes.
entries.subject: painted fishing pirogues and crowds at Tanji fish landing

entries.caption: Easy for Everybody
entries.description: Short flights, short distances, warm shallow sea and a country used to visitors.
entries.subject: children playing in shallow water on a Gambian beach

entries.caption: Birding on Foot
entries.description: Abuko, Tanji and the Kotu creek — three of the best birding walks in Africa, all near the beach.
entries.subject: birdwatchers with binoculars on a creek path at Kotu

entries.caption: Long Established
entries.description: Everything from big beach hotels to small river lodges, and forty years of practice.
entries.subject: a river lodge terrace looking out over the Gambia river

entries.caption: Community Birding
entries.description: Village guide associations have run the birding here for decades, and the money stays.
entries.subject: a local guide pointing out a bird to visitors on a creek

entries.caption: River Light
entries.description: The upper river at dawn, when the mist sits on the water and the fish eagles call.
entries.subject: mist on the Gambia river at dawn with a fish eagle

entries.caption: Kartong
entries.description: The far south, a river mouth, a crocodile pool and almost nobody.
entries.subject: the quiet river mouth and empty beach at Kartong

entries.caption: Why The Gambia
entries.description: Six hundred bird species and four hundred years of river history, in a country you cross in a day.
entries.subject: a small boat on the Gambia river with mangrove either side
